system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: ivy.chen opened the macro-enabled document Statement.docm in Word; Word then spawned PowerShell under ivy.chen's account.

The PowerShell command used hidden-window and no-profile options, with an encoded command that invokes a download-and-execute expression for https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1. The proxy recorded a successful HTTP 200 GET for that URL from PowerShell.
PowerShell spawned rundll32 to call Init in C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll; the rundll32 process ran for about ten seconds.
The document-to-hidden-PowerShell-to-downloaded-script-to-user-profile DLL execution chain is strongly indicative of malicious activity, rather than an ordinary visible PowerShell window.

Before ivy.chen's recorded interactive logon on WS-ICHEN-01, Kerberos records show sam.okafor tickets requested from the workstation's IP for WS-SOKAFOR-01, followed by a network logon for sam.okafor on WS-SOKAFOR-01 from that IP.
At 14:13 UTC, Kerberos records show leo.martins tickets requested from WS-ICHEN-01's IP for WS-NBLAKE-01, followed by a network logon for leo.martins on WS-NBLAKE-01 from that IP.
The sam.okafor and leo.martins network authentications from WS-ICHEN-01 are suspicious in this context, but the records alone do not establish who initiated them or whether they were authorized.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records show the download request and response status, but not the downloaded PowerShell script's contents.
The records identify the DLL path and rundll32 invocation, but do not provide the DLL contents, hash, signature, or resulting activity.
No PowerShell script-block, AMSI, or equivalent content-level telemetry is included to confirm the script's actions.
The proxy records establish an HTTP 200 response but do not include the response body.
The evidence covers only the stated review window; it does not establish activity before or after that period.
claims_not_established: The exact behavior or impact of u.ps1 and svchelper.dll, including whether they established persistence, stole data, or communicated with additional infrastructure.
Whether the sam.okafor and leo.martins authentications were initiated by the payload, by ivy.chen, or by authorized activity.
Whether any actions were performed in the AWS console or whether cloud resources or data were accessed.
Whether other hosts or accounts were compromised.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and analyze Statement.docm, u.ps1, and svchelper.dll; collect hashes, signatures, file metadata, and relevant endpoint artifacts.
Collect PowerShell operational/script-block logs, AMSI and Defender detections, and endpoint process, file, registry, and network telemetry for WS-ICHEN-01.
Review proxy transaction details and retrieve the exact downloaded script content if retained.
Investigate the sam.okafor authentication and WS-SOKAFOR-01 logon, and the leo.martins authentication and WS-NBLAKE-01 logon, using endpoint and domain-controller logs.
Contain WS-ICHEN-01 and assess/revoke potentially exposed sam.okafor and leo.martins credentials or sessions as appropriate.
